input.quote: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
input.rationale: Section 14 meets the preferred position in full. 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and independently developed IP, with no transfer to Vendor beyond a limited processing right (reinforced by 15.1's no-sale/no-advertising/no-model-training restriction and 1.8's exclusion of Customer Data from Vendor Technology). 14.2 vests ownership of each Deliverable in Customer on creation with an express present assignment from Vendor plus personnel assignments and further-assurances. 14.3 lets Vendor retain only its pre-existing Vendor Technology and back-stops embedded Vendor Technology with the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid, modify-and-derivative licence in 13.2 (sublicensable to Affiliates and contractors under 13.1/13.3). 14.4 negates joint ownership absent a separate signed instrument setting exploitation rights, and feedback use is limited to generalized suggestions with Customer retaining unrestricted rights in its own feedback. Nothing assigns Customer IP or data to Vendor, so no walk-away trigger. Minor, non-material notes only: ownership in 14.2 is conditioned on payment of Fees; "Deliverable" (1.4) captures only work product an Order Form identifies as created specifically for Customer; 1.3 carves anonymized, non-linkable operational telemetry out of Customer Data; and 14.1's processing right extends to "improve the Services for Customer" (bounded by 15.1). None of these warrants a redline.
